rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Nine phyla, nine body plans. Sponges filter water through choanocyte-lined canals at the cellular grade; cnidarians sting with cnidoblasts as diploblastic radials; flatworms flatten as acoelomates; roundworms round out as pseudocoelomates with a complete gut; annelids segment with true metamerism and nephridia; arthropods joint their chitinous armour and tagmatize into Crustacea, Myriapoda, Insecta and Arachnida;…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Pores, stings, flat, round, rings, joints, shell, tube feet, notochord.
Annelid classes: many bristles, few bristles, leech.
Chordate quartet: notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, gill slits, post-anal tail.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Spongilla is a sponge that lives in fresh water. Marine life is not the diagnostic character of Porifera. Pores and choanocytes are.  ·  Hydra is a cnidarian even though it lives in fresh water and has no medusa. Anthozoa also have no medusa. The class still stands.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Aschelminthes is the syllabus name. Nematoda is the class name used for Ascaris and Wuchereria.  ·  Pelecypoda and Bivalvia are the same class. Either label is acceptable with Unio as the example.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Peripatus*** — connecting link Annelida–Arthropoda.  ·  ***Pila, Unio, Octopus*** — the three molluscan classes.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Life cycles of Plasmodium, earthworm and frog are separate notes. This note is the classification grid only.  ·  Orders and families are out of scope. Stop at class.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Make a nine-row table: phylum, diagnostic character, one class, one example.  ·  Add a second line under Annelida and Arthropoda for the class characters only.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Sponges filter, cnidarians sting, flatworms flatten, roundworms round, annelids segment, arthropods join, molluscs shell, echinoderms pump, chordates chord."

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **One phylum, one body plan:** each phylum's diagnostic characters (cnidoblasts, metamerism, jointed appendages, mantle, water vascular system, notochord) are structural inventions that define a whole radiation of species.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Porifera: cellular grade, canal system, choanocytes; Calcarea, Hexactinellida, Demospongiae.  ·  Cnidaria: diploblastic, cnidoblasts, polyp/medusa; Hydrozoa, Scyphozoa, Anthozoa.  ·  Platyhelminthes: acoelomate, flame cells; Turbellaria, Trematoda, Cestoda. Aschelminthes: pseudocoelom, complete gut — Nematoda, Rotifera.  ·  Annelida: metamerism, nephridia, closed circulation — Polychaeta, Oligochaeta, Hirudinea.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Arthropoda is the largest animal phylum — over a million described species, mostly insects.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Choanocytes identify → A  ·  Taenia is placed in → C

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Nine Phyla Up to Class The syllabus requires the diagnostic features and classification up to class of the major phyla: Porifera, Coelenterata (Cnidaria), Platyhelminthes, Aschelminthes, Annelida, Arthropoda, Mollusca, Echinodermata and Chordata. Each phylum is recognised by its body plan (Topic 41) plus a few diagnostic characters.  ·  ## 2. Phylum-by-Phylum Diagnostic Features and Classes ### 2.1 Porifera (sponges) - Cellular grade; asymmetrical; pore-bearing body with **canal system** (ascon, sycon, leucon); **choanocytes** (collar cells) create water currents; skeleton of spicules/spongin; larvae free-swimming.…  ·  ```svg Nine phyla — the body-plan tree <svg viewBox="0 0 640 380" font-family="Segoe UI" font-size="13"><rect x="0" y="0" width="640" height="380" fill="#ffffff"/><text x="320" y="28" text-anchor="middle" font-size="19" font-weight="bold" fill="#14161a">Nine phyla, one logic: tissue → cavity → coelom</text><rect x="40" y="60" width="120" height="60" rx="10"…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Arthropoda: jointed appendages, chitinous exoskeleton, ecdysis, open circulation — Crustacea, Myriapoda, Insecta, Arachnida.  ·  Mollusca: foot, visceral hump, mantle, radula, open circulation — Gastropoda, Bivalvia, Cephalopoda.  ·  Echinodermata: water vascular system with tube feet; pentamerous adult symmetry — Asteroidea, Ophiuroidea, Echinoidea, Holothuroidea, Crinoidea.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Chordata: notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, pharyngeal gill slits, post-anal tail — Pisces, Amphibia, Reptilia, Aves, Mammalia.  ·  A leech is an annelid without setae. Losing setae does not move it into the flatworms. It still has segments, a coelom and suckers.  ·  Octopus is a mollusc. The shell is reduced. The mantle, the arms made from the foot, and the radula keep it in Cephalopoda.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Phylum questions in 2023 and 2024 asked for features + classes + examples — three-part answers.  ·  "A phylum is a body plan that worked."  ·  Why do arthropods need to moult while annelids do not? **Answer.** The arthropod's **chitinous exoskeleton is a rigid armour** — excellent for protection and muscle leverage, but it **cannot grow**.…
